paragraph: Condos and townhouses are the Cliffside Park market with 88 sales over six months at a median of $553,000, and the category splits roughly seventy condo units to eighteen townhouses. The typical sale is a two-bedroom, two-bath unit, but prices run from $273,500 to $1,360,000 depending on the building and whether you are buying a Hudson River view, so the median is the number to anchor on. With a sale-to-list ratio slightly under asking, about 31 percent of sales going above list, and a median of 28.5 days on market, this tier is competitive but not frenzied. Expect competition on the good ones. Monthly closings climbed from 11 in February to 22 in July, which is the normal build into summer, and the median bounced between $441,000 and $718,000 month to month on mix rather than any real price move. Single-family is thin at 14 sales, median $825,000, mostly three-bedroom colonials, with a median 64.5 days on market and only two homes going above asking. Sellers there are okay waiting for the right buyer rather than pricing to move fast. Co-ops are the entry point at a median of $280,000 across five sales, and they carry board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction that not every buyer is aware of going in. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo, or the lower price point of a co-op.
